assertionResults.reason: While one `up` invocation was still running, a second concurrent `up` returned immediate lockfile error and exit code 1; after the first run finished, `down` succeeded, showing lock release.
With tier port 8101 occupied, startup did not emit `Port ... already in use by PID ...`; it attempted tier launch and later reported health-check timeout instead of explicit port-owner detection.
In the same partial-failure run, `fast` failed while `standard` and `litellm` came up healthy, confirming remaining tiers still start and mixed status is surfaced.

Re-running `up` with active services produced an `already running` summary and unchanged PIDs; with stale PID files injected, startup reported stale cleanup and replaced dead PIDs with fresh running processes.
Before startup, `up` warned that estimated memory (126.0 GB) exceeded available memory (87.6 GB); startup continued and all tier/litellm PID files were created.

With OpenRouter key configured, dry-run masked the key (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY=***`), runtime litellm command line contained no key literal, process environment exposed `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and logs contained no secret.

frictions.description: Port-conflict simulation required a longer timeout because startup attempted to launch on the occupied port and only failed after health-check timeout, rather than immediate conflict skip.
frictions.resolution: Increased test command timeout to allow full failure path completion and captured explicit timeout behavior for assertion adjudication.

frictions.description: Dependency check emits non-blocking litellm version mismatch warning on each up run (installed v1.82.6 vs pinned v1.67.2).
frictions.resolution: Treated warning as informational and proceeded because it did not prevent exercising assigned lifecycle assertions.

summary: Tested 6 assigned assertions: 5 passed, 1 failed (VAL-UP-012). No assertions were blocked.
